regime.summary: Policy rate held at 10.5% but the bill curve prices hikes, CPI is rising and Brent is up 83% in three months: an oil shock for an importer. KMI fell 8.4% in 3m and has rebounded 7% in 1m, so part of the fear is priced. Hike risk is the main unknown; the closest analogue is the 2021-22 tightening where the median stock fell 52%.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 10.5%; last MPC decision 2026-03-09: hold (+0bp)
Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate +0.97pp (market pricing hikes); CPI rising over 3 months (+1.7pp)
Tightening plus external stress: rate up 800bp in ten months with CPI above it. To June 2023 the median liquid stock fell 52% and 4 of 95 names rose.

core.thesis: Refinery sitting at its 252-day high (dist -0.1%) while most sectors fell over 3m; +16% 3m and +27% 6m into an oil shock. P/E 8.1. Open business question: refining margin sustainability and policy. Held as the oil-linked resting place, not as a trade.

Sponsor-led holding company within 4.6% of its 252-day high, +66% over 12m, P/E 9.7, up 11% over 3m against a falling market. Latest EPS yoy is -16.6%, treated as the open business question (one-offs vs earning power), not a reason to leave. Annual accounts transmitted 2026-04-07.

evidence.quote: Transmission of Annual Financial Statements for the Year Ended December 31,

core.thesis: Largest Islamic bank franchise in the pack, near its high (-3.5%), +113% over 12m and +6.7% over 3m while Islamic banks as a sector fell 13%. Rising rates are not a threat to a bank. EPS yoy -14% and a board notice with closed period are the watch points; half weight for that reason.

evidence.quote: 2026-04-10 MEBL: NOTICE OF BOARD MEETING AND CLOSED PERIOD - MEEZAN BANK LIMITED

watch.subject: Next SBP MPC decision
watch.trigger: A hike (the curve already prices one) cuts exposure toward 30 percent; a hold with Brent falling lifts the book back to the 75 percent default.

watch.subject: KSE100 and Brent oil shock
watch.trigger: Brent rolls over from 119 and the index holds the 1m rebound on a pullback; re-add toward the default core then.

watch.subject: ACPL offer letters
watch.trigger: Terms of the offer disclosed; judge what fraction of a holding the offer buys and the stub value before any entry.

evidence.quote: Material Information - Circulation of offer letters

watch.subject: CRTM
watch.trigger: Watch only: five locks and +84% in 1m, but the measured result for this type is nothing; act only if a filing explains it.

watch.subject: INIL
watch.trigger: EPS yoy +489% while P/E is 26 and price is 29% under its high; needs consolidated, one-off-stripped earnings from the accounts before it becomes an entry.

watch.subject: Foreign selling and mutual fund buying
watch.trigger: Foreign corporates sold 37mn USD in 20 sessions; if the 5-session mutual fund buying persists and foreigners stop selling, raise exposure.

exposure_reason: 50 percent rather than the 75 percent default because the bill curve prices a hike the SBP has not made, CPI is rising and Brent is up 83 percent, the same shape as the tightening-plus-external-stress episode where the median stock fell 52 percent. The core is tilted to oil-linked and bank names that gain or hold up in that case. I stay half invested because the index already fell 9.9 percent in 3m and rebounded, and mpc_hold has been positive over 60 sessions. The other 50 percent is dry powder for a post-decision entry, not a call that nothing is worth owning.
not_known: FX reserves, current account and IMF status are not in the bundle. No SBP meeting date, no read on whether Brent is spiking or sustained, and no consolidated one-off-stripped EPS for the core names.
contamination_note: No knowledge of events after 2026-04-10 was used. The base_rates.csv warning about post-date measurement was noted, and rows were used only as rough odds for a situation type.
